data.title: Copper Rises on Potential Technical Rebound — Market Talk
data.description: Copper rises in early Asia trade, after tumbling to its lowest level in seven months in the previous session. The metal is one of the beneficiaries of the artificial-intelligence investment boom, ANZ Research analysts say in a note. The rapid expansion of data centers, along with the generation and grid infrastructure needed to power them, has shifted expectations for copper consumption. However, a wave of selling hit commodity markets recently, as risk appetite was weighed by concerns that this year's AI-related rally across equity markets has been overdone, they add. The three-month copper futures contract on the London Metal Exchange rises 1.5% to $12,661.00 a metric ton. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: China Stock Market May Test Resistance At 3,600 Points
data.description:
BEIJING (dpa-AFX) - The China stock market on Wednesday snapped the four-day losing streak in which it had slumped almost 100 points or 2.7 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,590-point plateau and it may see additional support on Thursday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is murky, with Middle East tensions likely offset by sinking crude oil prices and bargain hunting among the technology stocks. The European markets were down and the U.S. bourses were mixed and the Asian markets figure to split the difference.

The SCI finished slightly higher on Wednesday as gains from the technology energy and finance sectors were offset be weakness from the retail and health stocks.

For the day, the index perked 3.25 points or 0.09 percent to finish at 3,587.83 after trading between 3,560.45 and 3,596.55. The Shenzhen Composite Index fell 6.71 points or 0.33 percent to end at 2,028.26.

The lead from Wall Street is weak as the major averages opened mixed but turned lower before recovering in the afternoon to finish mixed.

The Dow tumbled 561.25 points or 1.11 percent to finish at 50,198.17, while the NASDAQ climbed 101.50 points or 0.42 percent to close at 24,429.88 and the S&P 500 fell 16.90 points or 0.23 percent to end at 7,323.63.

The choppy trading on Wall Street came as traders digested earnings news from AI giant and market leader Nvidia (NVDA), which reported better than expected fiscal third quarter results and raised its revenue guidance.

Investors may also have been looking forward to Claude developer Anthropic's initial public offering later this week.

Gold stocks showed a substantial move to the downside, while pharmaceutical, healthcare and banking stocks also saw considerable weakness.

Crude oil prices tumbled on Wednesday following a report that U.S. crude oil inventories increased much more than expected in the last week. West Texas Intermediate crude for December delivery was down $2.92 or 3.4 percent to $83.09 a barrel.

data.description:

Palm oil may test a support at 4,334 ringgit per metric ton, a break below could trigger a fall into the 4,204-4,276 ringgit range.

The bounce caused by the support looks very weak, as it ended around a resistance at 4,392 ringgit. The weakness signals an extension of the fall toward 4,276 ringgit.

A break above 4,392 ringgit may lead to a gain to 4,463 ringgit. On the daily chart, the contract has pierced below the support at 4,368 ringgit, which looks unable to hold.

The next support will be at 4,292 ringgit, a break below which could open the way toward 4,210 ringgit.

data.title: Bitcoin Gains Ground But Outlook Remains Cautious — Market Talk
data.description: Bitcoin rises 1.5% in Asia as sentiment gets a small lift from Anthropic's IPO. The company sold more shares than planned at a higher price than expected, sending a welcome signal about demand for AI trades after waves of selloffs. E-mini Nasdaq futures rose 1.4% after the IPO terms were announced. A rebound in tech would bode well for crypto, which has tracked AI and tech stocks recently due to parallels as gauges of risk appetite and sensitivity to interest rates. Bitcoin's gains are particularly notable in the wake of Fed minutes underlining hawkish expectations, but it remains around four-month lows. A sustainable recovery hinges on improving institutional demand, easing monetary expectations and evidence that leveraged selling pressure has subsided, says Zaye Capital Markets. Bitcoin was last at $63,219. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

data.title: Jeju Air to Benefit From Expanded South Korea-China FTA — Market Talk
data.description: Jeju Air stands to benefit from the expanded South Korea-China free-trade agreement, Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn says. Earlier this week, Seoul and Beijing reached a deal after years of negotiations to broaden the scope of their 2015 FTA to include sectors such as tourism, investment and financial services, during their leaders' bilateral summit on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China. data.title: Explained - Why gold prices have corrected 34% from record high levels this year
data.description:
Global gold prices continued to tumble on Wednesday, falling another 3%, after more hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve officials in their minutes and independently raised speculation of more aggressive tightening from the central bank to combat inflation.

Spot gold prices traded near $3,730 an ounce on Thursday, November 19, after a 3.2% drop overnight took prices to their lowest closing level since September 2025.

Minutes of the previous Fed policy released last night showed that nearly all officials said that rates will have to be raised in the months ahead to bring inflation back down to their 2% target.

Higher borrowing costs are negative for bullion prices as the yellow metal does not yield any interest.

Sentiments soured further when Fed Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC in an interview that inflation was headed in the wrong direction and that a larger, 50 basis points rate hike may have to be considered to bring prices down.

With Wednesday's fall, Gold prices in the spot market are down over 34% from their record high levels of close to $5,600 an ounce that the metal had surged to earlier this year.

However, the start of the US-Iran war in February-end brought about a spike in energy prices, which, in-turn put pressure on inflation, and therefore, central bank polices, which were in their easing stance at the start of the year, had to start tightening policy to combat the rising inflation. US CPI has remained above the Fed's 2% target for years now.

Adding further pressure on Gold prices is a stronger US Dollar, which is also due to fears of a tighter monetary policy. A stronger Dollar makes gold purchasing more expensive for foreign buyers.

The sell-off in AI stocks is also contributing to the volatility in prices as investors are selling positions elsewhere to cover up for these losses.

Along with Gold, Silver prices also tumbled over 5% overnight to nearly $45 an ounce, correcting from their peak levels of over $120 an ounce earlier this year. Platinum and Palladium are seeing modest gains this morning after edging lower overnight.

data.title: Metal Hawk Hits Bonanza Gold Grades at Leinster South Numbat Discovery
data.description:
Metal Hawk has struck its richest gold grades yet at Leinster South in Western Australia, with fresh drilling confirming a high-grade discovery at the Numbat shear.

The standout intercept delivered 11 metres grading 48.3 grams per tonne gold from 103m, including a spectacular 6m at 81.2g/t.

Other holes returned 4m at 28.5g/t and a broader 27m at 5.7g/t, giving the explorer several strong results across the southern Thylacine area.

Far from being confined to the quartz lode that first drew attention to Numbat, the gold is turning up in the surrounding rock, prompting Metal Hawk to extend its diamond drilling campaign.

Building on Earlier Hits

The new assays come from a September reverse circulation program of 10 holes totalling 1,642m, including five aimed directly at the shear following an encouraging earlier intersection.

That earlier hit of 4m at 12.5g/t was followed about 60m farther down the structure by the new 11m intercept, strengthening the emerging picture of high-grade gold below the original find.

In a separate hole, the 4m at 28.5g/t interval included 2m at 56.2g/t, while another returned gold as deep as 192m, where 10m graded 1.4g/t.

The broader 27m result included 7m at 12.6g/t, with further lower-grade mineralisation continuing to the end of the hole.

Gold in the shear is closely associated with bismuth and tellurium, two elements the exploration team can use to help trace further high-grade zones.

Extends Beyond Quartz

For much of the exploration at Leinster South, the richest gold had appeared in quartz veins, making the Numbat quartz lode a natural target for follow-up drilling.

The September campaign changed that picture by repeatedly finding gold in the sheared dolerite and gabbro around the veins, including significant intersections in every hole drilled beneath the earlier shear discovery.

That wider distribution has led Metal Hawk to investigate whether the original lode is one part of a more extensive gold-bearing system rather than an isolated concentration.

“While our initial focus was the Numbat quartz lode, drilling has revealed a broader zone of high-grade mineralisation, indicating that the Numbat lode may form part of a much larger mineralised system,” managing director Will Belbin said.

"With diamond drilling already underway to test the zone along strike and at depth, our priority is to understand the geometry and scale of the Numbat shear and assess its potential to host multiple high-grade gold shoots.”

Drilling Program Ongoing

Diamond drilling began at Thylacine South in early November with about 1,200m initially planned, but the latest assays have persuaded Metal Hawk to keep the rigs working until the end of the year.

The expanded program will test the Numbat shear along its length and farther underground, seeking to establish how the high-grade zones fit together, with attention also turning to the southern margin of the Thylacine Gabbro, where the company plans to pursue similar gold indicators beyond the current discovery.

The broader Leinster South project—which includes the Thylacine, Tysons and Siberian Tiger prospects—spans more than 430 square kilometres south of Leinster, as the name implies.

After its first drilling at Leinster South in 2025, Metal Hawk now has its highest-grade gold hits in hand and a longer campaign underway to probe their extent.

data.title: Anthropic raises $3 billion from Japanese investors in IPO, lower end of the range
data.description:
Anthropic PBC has raised around $3 billion, as part of its initial public offering from Japanese investors, the lower end of its planned range, as per a regulatory filing.

The Claude chatbox maker has sold 36.1 million Class A shares in its Japanese tranche post pricing its IPO at $83 apiece, which is above the marketed range. This was below the 38.5 million to 50 million shares it had estimated to sell, with the Japan portion initially estimated to raise $3 billion to $3.5 billion.

Japan is among the few places where household buyers have direct access to the IPO. This also offered the much required support for the country's capital markets. With around a month to go, the IPO proceeds in 2026 are so far below than any full year since 2011 in yen terms, Bloomberg reported.

Anthropic's Japan follows Elon Musk's SpaceX IPO in June, which also tapped the nation's pool of capital. Such transactions, called public offering sans listing, have helped in raising the Mizuho Financial Group Inc's profile as coordinator of global deals.

The AI firm and its seven co-founders have raised $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement. It sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders sold 23.6 million shares.

With inputs from Bloomberg

data.title: Fiji declares state of disaster amid El Nino-driven drought
data.description:
Fiji has declared a national state of disaster after an El Nino-driven drought caused widespread water shortages, with the Pacific nation's weather bureau forecasting below-normal rainfall until at least April.

In a national address on Wednesday, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said the declaration would allow his government to scale up its response by mobilising resources and coordinating assistance as conditions continue to worsen.

"Families across Fiji are concerned about the availability of water and the effects of prolonged dry conditions on their daily lives," Rabuka said.

"Farmers are worried about their crops and livestock, while communities, particularly in remote and maritime areas, face growing pressure on their water supplies. These concerns are real."

Rabuka said his government has set aside 20 million Fiji dollars ($8.5 million) for the national response, redeployed from existing funds, to ensure emergency water supplies for families and farmers.

The state of disaster has been declared for one month, with the government able to extend or revoke it based on the advice of the National Disaster Risk Management Council.

El Nino is a natural climate pattern in which surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become unusually warm, causing weather extremes around the world, including drought in some regions and flooding in others. Some scientists say global warming may increase its intensity.

The US Climate Prediction Center said last week that El Nino is strengthening, with a greater than 79% chance of a strong-to-very-strong event through January to March. Australia in June said El Nino could intensify in the second half of 2026 to become one of the strongest in seven decades.

Fiji's national weather bureau warned in October that strong El Nino conditions persist across the tropical Pacific.

Rainfall is likely to remain below normal from November through April, while daytime temperatures are expected to exceed normal levels through January across most of the country, the Fiji Meteorological Service said.

($1 = 2.3436 Fiji dollars)
